# Christmas Cards

## Overview
Christmas cards are one of the most recognizable holiday traditions, blending personal connection, creativity, and nostalgia. Whether handmade, store‑bought, photo‑based, or digital, cards have evolved from Victorian innovations into a modern industry that still sends over a billion cards each year in the United States. Even with declining mail volume, Christmas cards remain a meaningful way to share holiday cheer, memories, and personalized messages.

---

## History of Christmas Cards

### Early Origins
The earliest known Christmas‑like greeting was sent in **1534**, but the first item resembling a Christmas card appeared in **1611**, created for King James I of England. It was a large, ornate manuscript folded into panels and decorated with a rose motif. [ C](https://www.whychristmas.com/customs/christmas-cards?copilot_analytics_&citationMarker=9F742443-6C92-4C44-BF58-8F5A7C53B6F1)

![[first-card.jpg|300]]
*First Christmas Card was made for King James[D]( https://historiclondontours.com/tales-of-london/f/the-man-who-invented-christmascards)

The first *commercial* Christmas card was commissioned in **1843** by Sir Henry Cole, a British civil servant who helped establish the Uniform Penny Post. He was overloaded with letters and it would have been rude not to respond to each one.  Cole asked artist **John Callcott Horsley** to design a card that could be printed and mailed easily. The card featured a family toasting in the center panel and charitable scenes on the sides. Cole printed 1,000 copies and sold the extras for one shilling each. [ D]( https://historiclondontours.com/tales-of-london/f/the-man-who-invented-christmascards)

### Expansion and Popularity
By the late 19th century, advances in chromolithography and mass printing helped Christmas cards spread across Britain and the United States. American printer **Louis Prang** popularized elaborate, colorful cards in the 1870s, helping establish the greeting card industry. [ G](https://grokipedia.com/page/Christmas_card?copilot_analytics_metadata=eyJldmVudEluZm9fY29udmVyc2F0aW9uSWQiOiJaNXJNRnc4UlhGUmFCaWk3S0RpOFQiLCJldmVudEluZm9fY2xpY2tEZXN0aW5hdGlvbiI6Imh0dHBzOlwvXC9ncm9raXBlZGlhLmNvbVwvcGFnZVwvQ2hyaXN0bWFzX2NhcmQiLCJldmVudEluZm9fbWVzc2FnZUlkIjoiU3ZtTGhzOEpCZlg5azFxcUszVG1qIiwiZXZlbnRJbmZvX2NsaWNrU291cmNlIjoiY2l0YXRpb25MaW5rIn0%3D&citationMarker=9F742443-6C92-4C44-BF58-8F5A7C53B6F1)

Victorian cards often featured:
- Nativity scenes
- Robins and winter landscapes
- Santa Claus and evergreen imagery
- Charity‑themed illustrations

By the early 1900s, Christmas cards were a widespread tradition across Europe and North America. [ C](https://www.whychristmas.com/customs/christmas-cards?copilot_analytics_&citationMarker=9F742443-6C92-4C44-BF58-8F5A7C53B6F1)

## Handmade vs. Store‑Bought Cards

### Handmade Cards
Handmade cards have existed since the earliest days of the tradition. Before mass printing, cards were:
- hand‑drawn
- hand‑colored
- embroidered or sewn
- decorated with paper cutouts

A 1916 example shows a hand‑sewn card preserved in museum collections. [ B](https://www.thecollector.com/history-christmas-cards/?copilot_analytics_%3D%3D&citationMarker=9F742443-6C92-4C44-BF58-8F5A7C53B6F1)

Today, handmade cards remain popular for:
- scrapbooking styles
- watercolor illustrations
- calligraphy
- mixed‑media designs
- personalized keepsakes

### Store‑Bought Cards
Store‑bought cards became mainstream after the 1843 Horsley design and exploded in popularity with:
- chromolithography (1870s)
- mass‑market printing (early 1900s)
- Hallmark’s rise in the 1910s–1920s

![[christmas-cards.jpeg]]
Modern store‑bought cards include:
- boxed sets
- charity cards
- pop‑up cards
- foil‑stamped and embossed designs
- humorous or pop‑culture themes

---

## Photo Cards
Photo cards emerged in the mid‑20th century as photography became more accessible. Today they are one of the most popular formats, especially for families who want to share:
- yearly portraits
- baby or pet photos
- travel highlights
- milestone updates

Photo cards blend the tradition of holiday greetings with modern personalization, and they remain a major part of the U.S. greeting card market. [ G](https://grokipedia.com/page/Christmas_card?copilot_analytics_metadata=eyJldmVudEluZm9fY29udmVyc2F0aW9uSWQiOiJaNXJNRnc4UlhGUmFCaWk3S0RpOFQiLCJldmVudEluZm9fY2xpY2tTb3VyY2UiOiJjaXRhdGlvbkxpbmsiLCJldmVudEluZm9fY2xpY2tEZXN0aW5hdGlvbiI6Imh0dHBzOlwvXC9ncm9raXBlZGlhLmNvbVwvcGFnZVwvQ2hyaXN0bWFzX2NhcmQiLCJldmVudEluZm9fbWVzc2FnZUlkIjoiU3ZtTGhzOEpCZlg5azFxcUszVG1qIn0%3D&citationMarker=9F742443-6C92-4C44-BF58-8F5A7C53B6F1)

## USPS and Christmas Cards

### How Much Mail Christmas Cards Generate
The USPS handles enormous holiday mail volume each year. While exact Christmas‑card‑only numbers are not published, the U.S. sends **approximately 1.3 billion Christmas cards annually**, making them a major contributor to holiday mail traffic. [ G](https://grokipedia.com/page/Christmas_card?copilot_analytics_metadata=eyJldmVudEluZm9fY2xpY2tTb3VyY2UiOiJjaXRhdGlvbkxpbmsiLCJldmVudEluZm9fY2xpY2tEZXN0aW5hdGlvbiI6Imh0dHBzOlwvXC9ncm9raXBlZGlhLmNvbVwvcGFnZVwvQ2hyaXN0bWFzX2NhcmQiLCJldmVudEluZm9fbWVzc2FnZUlkIjoiU3ZtTGhzOEpCZlg5azFxcUszVG1qIiwiZXZlbnRJbmZvX2NvbnZlcnNhdGlvbklkIjoiWjVyTUZ3OFJYRlJhQmlpN0tEaThUIn0%3D&citationMarker=9F742443-6C92-4C44-BF58-8F5A7C53B6F1)

### USPS Holiday Season Revenue
Holiday mail is considered the USPS “peak season,” generating significant revenue and requiring expanded staffing and logistics. USPS reports that peak season is a prime opportunity to attract customers and boost loyalty. [ H](https://www.uspsoig.gov/reports/audit-reports/service-performance-during-fiscal-year-2026-peak-mailing-season?copilot_analytics_%3D%3D&citationMarker=9F742443-6C92-4C44-BF58-8F5A7C53B6F1)

### Decline in Mailed Cards

Mail volume has been declining for nearly two decades. First‑Class Mail — which includes greeting cards — has dropped **50% between 2008 and 2023**, falling from 92 billion pieces to 46 billion. The primary cause is “electronic diversion,” meaning people now use email, texting, and social media instead of physical mail. [ E](https://www.uspsoig.gov/reports/white-papers/analysis-historical-mail-volume-trends?copilot_analytics_%3D&citationMarker=9F742443-6C92-4C44-BF58-8F5A7C53B6F1)

A separate USPS analysis shows first‑class mail volume has dropped **57% over the past 20 years**, reflecting the same trend. [ F](https://www.wmur.com/article/usps-financial-viability-congress-action/73249258?copilot_analytics_&citationMarker=9F742443-6C92-4C44-BF58-8F5A7C53B6F1)

Despite this decline, Christmas cards remain one of the strongest surviving forms of personal correspondence because the hold emotional and nostalgic value.

## Why Christmas Cards Declined

- Rise of digital communication  
- Social media holiday posts  
- E‑cards and digital newsletters  
- Rising postage costs  
- Convenience of texting or messaging  
- Younger generations preferring digital formats  

---
## Christmas Cards as Gifts

Christmas cards can be gifts themselves, especially when they include:

- handwritten letters
- family updates
- personal artwork
- photo memories
- small keepsakes (pressed flowers, bookmarks, stickers)
- handmade embellishments

Many people save cards for scrapbooks, memory boxes, or holiday displays, making them long‑lasting sentimental items.
